purpose: Timestamped opening and closing prices for every market originated, so a later backtest can score the decision that was available at the time rather than the number that hindsight prefers.

moneyline_method.formula: p_home = Phi(fair_spread_home / sigma); American odds inverted from p
moneyline_method.sigma_source: residual SD of the walk-forward backtest in data/verified/backtest.json
moneyline_method.note: Using a measured residual SD rather than the 13.5-point convention in the hub params. Ties (an exact push on the spread) are not a moneyline outcome; pushes have zero probability in the continuous normal, so the ML is not adjusted for them.

third_party_reference.source: commercial odds page cited in that file
third_party_reference.reason: not an official NFL source; single undated snapshot with no open/close pair; excluded from all calculations by the project's official-sources-only rule

policy: Every market cell that has no official source is blank and marked UNVERIFIED.
Third-party prices are carried for transparency in their own columns and are excluded from every calculation, because the project uses officially sourced numbers only.
Our own line is an official record of our own output; it is not a market price and is never called one.
The close is defined as the last number recorded at or before kickoff. With no feed it stays blank, and a row with a blank close cannot contribute to a closing-line-value calculation.
